analysis:
All three changed files are Swift test files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests, so there is no production code change in this batch and no new attack surface. I found no regression against the threat model.

IdleCalibrationCoordinatorTests.swift (head lines 95-115) adds a test that a calibration session records what first cancelled it ('device work' vs 'request') and that a new session starts clean. It only exercises the coordinator's cancellation bookkeeping.

ModelCalibrationPolicyTests.swift (head lines 16-70) adds tests for the shape-warmup cells, the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP kill switch, and the shader-cache cold-detection heuristic. The tests assert that a non-affirmative value ('0', 'false', 'off', 'no') disables warmup. They also assert that LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvironment passes the variable through. The env var is a performance/TTFT-calibration control with no authorization, attestation or secrecy role. The warmup likely uses synthetic prompts, but that is not verifiable from the supplied test files.

StartupPreloadTests.swift adds event-ordering tests (load, selftest, warmup) and a shapeWarmup dependency. The tests confirm that warmup runs only after a passing self-test and that fail-closed retirement still excludes models from the loaded set. The ordering is consistent with the fail-closed self-test semantics already in the file.

Remaining questions sit outside the supplied evidence. I could not see the production implementations: StartupPreloader.shapeWarmup, ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup, and the IdleCalibrationCoordinator cancellationSource. A later pass should check whether the warmup runs prompts with real consumer content or touches the prefix cache (T-041, TB-007). It should also check that warmup output cannot feed prefix-cache donation or telemetry in a way that leaks data (A-001, T-028). The test files themselves show no such behavior. The StartupPreloadTests patch excerpt and the file are truncated, so the later tests were not seen.
